agree.reason: Opening with Dana's own $600K quote and giving a clear price and setup time could get her to take a call, but nothing in it would help her get her protective IT director on board.

honest.reason: The 4.1-to-1.9 drop is reported accurately as one customer's result, but showing only the best of six customers, with no mention of the 2.8-to-2.2 result, implies halving is typical when the facts don't support that.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the $75K annual cost correctly but never sets it against what a similar cut would save on her $600K (roughly $300K at half, about $125K even at the weaker 21%), which is the most persuasive figure available.

right_comparison.reason: The status quo of over $600K a year in returns comes up only as the opening hook and is never compared with the $75K price or with what happens if she does nothing.

qualification.reason: A claim resting on a single customer needs a hedge, such as results ranging from about 21% to 54% or a pilot at one site with a checkable error-rate target, and the email offers none.

objections.reason: Saying it sits on top of the WMS rather than replacing it partly answers the IT worry, but the email says nothing about how much IT work or integration is involved, and that is exactly what the resistant director will ask.

fit.reason: It is short, easy to scan on a phone, and has a specific subject line and a single clear request.
